tour.name: Bike Tour 26
tour.subtitle: Canberra, the Central West, Blue Mountains, Southern Highlands and South Coast

p: Lanyon Shops car park, same as last year. 8:30 am coffee and catch-up, 9:00 am departure.
Refuel at the end of each day. Longest gap between fuel stops is 183 km.
Couples in queens, everyone else in twins. Dinners booked at all three by Gary G; see Dinners.
li: Barrack Point Holiday Park, Jason Ave, Barrack Point
Huskisson Beach Motel, 9 Hawke St, Huskisson
Sweep stays at the rear unless a new sweep is named.
Don’t turn at an intersection unless you can see the rider behind you.
Lost? Call Tony, then Ewart, then Gary G. Numbers are in WhatsApp.

p: Puncture kit with air, cable ties, Allen keys, spanners, nuts and bolts, screwdrivers, fuses, chain lube. First aid kit; confirm who is trained.
Service, tyres and pressures, chain lube, mirrors, tight bolts (especially Harleys), oil and water, brake pads, lever adjustment, charged battery, comms and nav set up.

tour.meet: Lanyon Shops car park, 8:30 am coffee, 9:00 am departure

days.label: Ride down
days.title: Caringbah to Conder
days.feel: Mostly motorway; an easy afternoon run
days.roads: M1 and Picton Rd, Hume Motorway, Federal Hwy past Lake George, Tuggeranong Parkway. Distances and times are estimates; check them in a maps app.
days.fuelNote: Caringbah to Goulburn is about 190 km, just over the group’s 183 km rule. If your range is tight, top up at the Sutton Forest services on the Hume.

best.title: Goulburn to Conder
best.why: The Federal Highway runs along the edge of Lake George in the afternoon light, then the Tuggeranong Parkway brings you into the south of Canberra. Not technical, just a relaxed finish to the run down.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: Conder to Millthorpe
days.feel: Mostly cruisey with some tight sections
days.roads: Cotter, Brindabella and Mountain Creek roads, Wee Jasper, Wargeila and Rye Park, Lachlan Valley, Mid Western Hwy

best.title: Tharwa to Cavan
best.why: Cotter, Brindabella, Uriarra and Mountain Creek roads: the tightest riding of the day, with pine forest, river crossings and almost no traffic before the long open run north. Mountain Creek Rd is narrow, so keep it tidy.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Millthorpe to Shellharbour
days.roads: Vittoria Rd and Mitchell Hwy, Sofala and Castlereagh, Great Western Hwy, Mulgoa and Silverdale, Old Hume, Picton and Mt Keira

best.title: Bathurst to Ilford
best.why: Sofala Rd rolls and twists through gold-rush country and down to the Turon River. Coming straight after a lap of Mount Panorama, it’s the most fun hour of a long day. Runner-up: Mt Keira Rd, with the drop to the coast.

days.label: Day 3
days.title: Shellharbour to Huskisson
days.roads: Illawarra and Tourist roads, Moss Vale Rd, Kangaroo Valley Rd, Princes Hwy, Currarong and Jervis Bay roads

best.title: Fitzroy Falls to Kangaroo Valley
best.why: The Moss Vale Rd descent down Barrengarry Mountain is a run of tight switchbacks off the escarpment into the valley, ending over Hampden Bridge. On Option 2, Jamberoo Mountain Rd is the tighter, more technical bonus.

alt.label: Option 2 hectic loop
alt.feel: Mostly tight roads, more technical riding
alt.roads: Adds Jamberoo Rd, Illawarra Hwy, Pearsons Lane and Nowra Rd

days.label: Day 4
days.title: Huskisson to Theodore
days.feel: Mostly cruisey with some tight sections
days.roads: Huskisson, Pine Forest, Hawken and Turpentine roads, Braidwood Rd, Nerriga, Oallen, Sandy Point and Cullulla roads

best.title: Huskisson to Nerriga
best.why: Turpentine and Braidwood roads climb off the coast through empty forest onto the tablelands. It’s quiet, flowing riding with the morning still cool, before the cruise home.

days.label: Ride home
days.title: Huskisson to Caringbah
days.feel: Coastal cruising, then the best coast road in NSW
days.roads: Princes Hwy through Berry and Gerringong, M1 to Wollongong, Lawrence Hargrave Drive over Sea Cliff Bridge, Lady Wakehurst Drive through Royal National Park. Distances and times are estimates; check them in a maps app.
days.fuelNote: Huskisson to Caringbah is about 185 km, just over the 183 km rule. Top up in Wollongong.

best.title: Wollongong to Caringbah
best.why: Up the coast on Lawrence Hargrave Drive, over Sea Cliff Bridge, then the rainforest bends of Lady Wakehurst Drive through Royal National Park, finishing almost at your door. A park entry fee may apply.

stops.note: A midday start, arriving in Canberra the afternoon before so Day 1 starts fresh. Fuel up before you leave.
stops.audit: Leaving at noon, so a pie for the road is on. FLOUR (open until 2 pm) and Bourke Street are the picks, both a few minutes from home.
stops.fact: The name is said to come from a local Aboriginal word for the pademelon, a small wallaby.

stops.note: Wool city on the Hume, home of the Big Merino.
stops.audit: Trappers is the obvious late-lunch stop: open until 6 pm every day, with a big car park right by the highway exit.
stops.fact: Goulburn was Australia’s first inland city, proclaimed in 1863.

stops.ref: Day 1 starts here tomorrow, with coffee at 8:30 am at Lanyon Shops. See Day 1 for Lanyon bakeries.

stops.note: Same meeting point as last year. Lanyon Marketplace sits at the southern edge of Tuggeranong, a few minutes from the open country.
stops.audit: Only one true bakery at Lanyon itself, so the rest of this list is the best of Tuggeranong within 10 minutes.
stops.fact: The suburb is named after Charles Conder, one of the Heidelberg School impressionist painters.

breakfast.note: Coffee at 8:30 am, roll out at 9:00 am, all at Lanyon Marketplace.
items: In the marketplace, right by the car park. Reviewers rate the coffee five-star and the kitchen is quick even when full.
Grab-and-go if you’d rather eat standing by the bikes.

stops.note: The ACT’s oldest township, beside the Murrumbidgee and the 1895 Tharwa Bridge.
stops.audit: No bakery, but the general store bakes the kind of pie and lamington riders detour for.
stops.fact: The name Tharwa is taken from the local Aboriginal name for nearby Mount Tennent.

stops.road: Cotter Rd, Brindabella Rd, Uriarra Rd, Mountain Creek Rd
stops.note: Rural locality north-west of the ACT, reached by the Cotter loop and the twisty Mountain Creek Rd.
stops.audit: Farmland only. No bakeries, no shops. Save room for Yass.
stops.fact: Cavan Station on the Murrumbidgee was the Murdoch family’s country property for decades.

stops.note: Wool-town main street with verandahs along Comur St, on the Yass River.
stops.audit: Clementine is the standout and has been named among the regional bakeries worth driving for, but it only trades Thursday to Sunday. On a weekday, Yass Country Kitchen is the fallback.
stops.fact: Explorer Hamilton Hume settled here. His home, Cooma Cottage, still stands on the edge of town.

stops.note: Tiny village between Yass and Boorowa, now best known for the wind farm on the ridgeline.
stops.audit: No bakery in the village. The nearest good one is in Boorowa, about 25 km off route.
stops.fact: The turbines on the ridges belong to one of the largest wind farms in NSW.

stops.note: Lachlan River town known for its Japanese Garden and the 1944 POW breakout site.
stops.audit: Two bakeries on Kendal St. Mick’s is the clear pick, but it shuts at 2 pm on weekdays and 1 pm Saturday, so lunch needs to be on time.
stops.fact: Cowra’s Japanese Garden is the largest of its kind in the southern hemisphere.

stops.note: Small Central West town on the Belubula River, between Cowra and Bathurst.
stops.audit: One bakery, and a good one.
stops.fact: The wind farm on the hills outside town was one of the first built in NSW.

stops.note: Bluestone heritage village near Orange, all galleries, wine and old shopfronts.
stops.stay: Millthorpe Motel, 26 Victoria St. Dinner booked.
stops.audit: No dedicated bakery in the village. For the 7:30 am getaway, Millthorpe Providore opens at 6 am on weekdays and is a few doors from the motel.
stops.fact: The whole village is classified by the National Trust as a heritage site.

breakfast.note: Depart 7:30 am, with the Bathurst bakery stop 30 minutes later. Coffee here, breakfast in Bathurst works best.
items: Weekdays from 6 am, weekends from 7 am
23 Victoria St, a few doors from the motel. Seven Miles coffee and breakfast rolls. No toilets inside (heritage building).
Wed to Sun from 7 am, closed Mon and Tue
Proper sit-down breakfast, but 7 am is tight for a 7:30 roll-out. Staff are happy to do takeaway coffees.

stops.note: Gold-rush city and home of Mount Panorama. Slow lap first, then breakfast.
stops.audit: The best field of the trip, and almost all open by 6 or 7 am. Carah’s and FoodWeDo lead on pies.
stops.fact: Mount Panorama is a public road. Outside race weekends, anyone can lap it at 60 km/h.

stops.note: Small stop on the Castlereagh Hwy, reached via the old gold-country road through Sofala.
stops.audit: No bakery.
stops.fact: The road in passes Sofala, often called Australia’s oldest surviving gold-rush town.

stops.note: Coal and steel town at the western foot of the Blue Mountains, home of the Zig Zag Railway.
stops.audit: Thin pickings. Golden Sunshine is the one locals swear by.
stops.fact: The Lithgow Small Arms Factory has been making rifles here since 1912.

stops.note: Big western Sydney hub on the Nepean River. Lunch is booked at Penrith Leagues Club.
stops.audit: Lunch is at the Leagues Club, so this is one for an afternoon treat. Poles is the heavyweight.
stops.fact: Penrith Whitewater Stadium was built for the canoe slalom at the Sydney 2000 Olympics.

stops.note: Small Wollondilly town near the old Burragorang Valley road.
stops.audit: One bakery, and it’s a proper country one.
stops.fact: The road west of here once led into the Burragorang Valley, flooded to create Warragamba Dam.

stops.note: Historic Macarthur town on the Nepean, with a heritage main street along Argyle St.
stops.audit: Punches above its weight. B85 and Arta Atelier are worth a future dedicated visit.
stops.fact: John Macarthur’s merino flock at Camden Park helped found Australia’s wool industry.

stops.note: Heritage railway town known for the Mushroom Tunnel and the old stone viaduct.
stops.audit: Parkside is the pick in town. If time allows, Loop-Line Pies in Thirlmere is the regional legend.
stops.fact: The stone viaduct over Stonequarry Creek dates to 1867, among the oldest railway bridges still in use in NSW.

stops.note: Escarpment summit above Wollongong with one of the best coastal lookouts in NSW.
stops.audit: No bakery on the hill. The summit cafe does good coffee, gozleme and Arabic sweets.
stops.fact: Coal was first mined commercially in the Illawarra on Mount Keira’s slopes in 1849.

stops.note: Old harbour village with a new marina at Shell Cove, just south of Lake Illawarra.
stops.stay: Barrack Point Holiday Park, Jason Ave. Dinner booked.
stops.audit: Tahlia’s in the village is the morning pick before the 8:30 am departure. Queen St and Warilla are closest to Barrack Point.
stops.fact: The town is named after the huge shell middens early settlers found along the shore.

breakfast.note: Depart Barrack Point 8:30 am. Shellharbour Village is about 3 km away, on Addison St.
items: By the harbour. The best-rated breakfast in the village, beautifully presented.
Food arrives fast, which suits a group with a departure time. Vittoria coffee.
Weekdays from 6 am, Sat 6:30 am, Sun 7 am
Mary St. Fresh, seasonal menu and consistently good coffee.

stops.note: Highland locality at the top of Macquarie Pass.
stops.audit: No bakery.
stops.fact: Getting here means climbing Macquarie Pass, about 600 m of rainforest hairpins up the escarpment.

stops.note: Southern Highlands capital: tulips, the Bradman Museum and a long main street of cafes.
stops.audit: The deepest field on the tour. Gumnut is the institution; Fermento is the quieter, higher-rated option a few doors along.
stops.fact: Don Bradman learned his cricket here as a boy; the museum sits beside the oval named after him.

stops.note: Working Highlands town with a broad main street and the old Dunmore Hotel.
stops.audit: Kim Thi Hot Bread is the surprise of the audit: queues for banh mi and old-school pie prices.
stops.fact: The town is said to take its name from Jemmy Moss, an early stockman in the district.

stops.note: The 81 m falls in Morton National Park, with a visitor centre right by the road.
stops.audit: No bakery, but the cafe’s homemade pies are a pleasant surprise.
stops.fact: The falls are named after Governor Charles FitzRoy and drop 81 m into the Yarrunga Valley.

stops.note: Village in a green bowl below the escarpment, reached by the switchbacks down Barrengarry Mountain.
stops.audit: One bakery and it delivers. Vanilla slice and pepper pie are the orders.
stops.fact: Hampden Bridge, built in 1898, is Australia’s oldest suspension bridge still carrying traffic.

stops.note: Rainforest ridge road between Kangaroo Valley and Berry; the twistiest bit of the day.
stops.audit: No bakery. Eyes on the road.
stops.fact: The ridge road runs through pockets of subtropical rainforest that survive on the escarpment.

stops.note: Coastal town built around the Kiama Blowhole and its harbour.
stops.audit: Strong field. Slow Dough is the best but only Friday to Sunday mornings; Parfait is the all-rounder by Black Beach.
stops.fact: George Bass anchored here in 1797 and described the blowhole in his journal.

stops.note: Dairy village in a valley under the escarpment, start of the climb up Jamberoo Mountain Rd.
stops.audit: One patisserie, and the curry beef pie has fans.
stops.fact: Jamberoo Action Park has been sending people down waterslides here since 1980.

stops.note: Highland potato country on red volcanic soil, with the Big Potato on the main road.
stops.audit: Pie territory. The Pie Shop is the famous one; locals say Southern Rise is the better pie.
stops.fact: The farm scenes in the 1995 film Babe were shot in the hills around Robertson.

stops.note: Farmland plateau between Robertson and Fitzroy Falls, rolling down to Kangaroo Valley.
stops.audit: No bakery.
stops.fact: Fitzroy Falls Reservoir here is part of the Shoalhaven Scheme, which pumps water up the escarpment.

stops.note: North bank of the Shoalhaven River, facing Nowra.
stops.audit: Two traditional bakeries side by side on Meroo St. Flour Water Salt South Nowra is the artisan choice.
stops.fact: Bomaderry station is the end of the line for South Coast trains.

stops.road: Greenwell Point Rd, Coonemia Rd, Currarong Rd
stops.note: Quiet fishing village on the Beecroft Peninsula with rock pools and a creek-mouth beach.
stops.audit: No bakery. Zest is the reliable stop; Alma’s is a gem if the days line up.
stops.fact: The wreck of the SS Merimbula, which ran aground off Beecroft Head in 1928, still lies nearby.

stops.road: Currarong Rd, Princes Hwy, Jervis Bay Rd, Huskisson Rd
stops.note: Jervis Bay town of white sand and dolphin cruises. Home of the Husky pie.
stops.stay: Huskisson Beach Motel, 9 Hawke St. Dinner booked.
stops.audit: Breakfast before the 8:30 am departure: Huskisson Bakery opens 6:30 am daily. Kraken is the artisan pick if it’s Thursday to Sunday.
stops.fact: It’s named after William Huskisson, the British politician famous as the first widely reported railway fatality, in 1830.

stops.ref: See Day 3 for Huskisson bakeries. Justin peels off here and heads north; see his ride home below.

breakfast.note: Depart 8:30 am. All three are on Owen St, a short walk from the motel.
items: Locals’ favourite. Great coffee and fluffy focaccia.
Bacon and egg burger with chilli jam
Huge portions and a water view. Popular, but tables turn quickly.
Corner spot facing the water. Good value and quick for an early start.

stops.road: Huskisson Rd, Pine Forest Rd, Hawken Rd, Princes Hwy, Turpentine Rd, Braidwood Rd
stops.note: Bush crossroads on the tableland between the coast and Braidwood, with a historic pub and not much else.
stops.audit: No bakery. Heads up: the Nerriga Hotel is listed as opening 11 am, Wednesday to Sunday, so it will likely be shut at 9:30. Bring a snack from Huskisson.
stops.fact: The pub is a survivor of the 19th-century gold era, when this road carried diggers and coaches.

stops.road: Nerriga Rd, Oallen Rd, Sandy Point Rd, Cullulla Rd
stops.note: Heritage village on the edge of Lake George, half an hour from Canberra.
stops.audit: Gunna Doo is the institution and opens at 4 am. Last bakery of the tour.
stops.fact: Nearby Lake George is famous for vanishing, sometimes sitting dry for years at a time.

stops.note: Southern Tuggeranong suburb. Home.
stops.audit: For a celebratory finish, L’épi in Chisholm is 5 minutes away. Full Tuggeranong list is under Conder on Day 1.
stops.fact: The suburb is named after Ted Theodore, Queensland premier and later federal Treasurer.

stops.timeNote: Depart 8:30 am, as the crew heads west
stops.ref: See Day 3 for Huskisson bakeries. Grab breakfast before the farewells.

stops.note: Shoalhaven town of antique shops, old pubs and a very famous donut van.
stops.audit: Two icons a few doors apart: Milkwood for pastries and the Donut Van for hot cinnamon donuts. The van opens at 8:30 am, so you’ll be just in time.
stops.fact: The town takes its name from Alexander Berry, who set up one of the first European estates on the Shoalhaven.

stops.note: The Gong: steelworks, surf beaches and the escarpment rising behind the city.
stops.audit: Crois and Millers’ both sell out, so late morning is a gamble. Royal Bakery is the safe bet, open to 4 pm daily.
stops.fact: Sea Cliff Bridge, just north of town, opened in 2005 after rockfalls closed the old cliff road.

stops.road: Lawrence Hargrave Dr, Lady Wakehurst Dr
stops.ref: See the ride down for Caringbah bakeries. FLOUR is open until 2 pm for a welcome-home pastry.

bakeries.name: FLOUR coffee & doughroom
bakeries.hours: Daily 7 am to 2 pm
bakeries.why: Caringbah South. Queues out the door for focaccia, danishes and pies.

bakeries.name: Home Bakery and Café
bakeries.hours: Mon to Sat 7:30 am to 3 pm, Sun from 9 am
bakeries.why: Willarong Rd. Fair prices and very friendly staff.

bakeries.name: Vu’s Bakehouse Caringbah
bakeries.hours: Weekdays 7 am to 6 pm, weekends to 4 pm
bakeries.why: Kingsway. Homemade pies, artisan sourdough and fresh banh mi.

bakeries.name: The Family Bakehouse
bakeries.hours: Daily from 6 am (weekends to 1:30 pm)
bakeries.why: Port Hacking Rd. Old-school bread, cupcakes and sweets.

bakeries.name: Bourke Street Bakery Caringbah
bakeries.hours: Tue to Fri from 5:30 am, Mon and weekends from 7 am
bakeries.why: Cawarra Rd. The earliest opener, with good pies and pastries.

bakeries.name: Trappers Bakery
bakeries.hours: Daily 5:30 am to 6 pm
bakeries.why: Next to the Big Merino. Huge range, barista coffee and an open fire in winter.

bakeries.name: Goulburn Bakery
bakeries.hours: Mon to Sat from 5 am, closed Sun
bakeries.why: Auburn St. A solid old-school bakery with pastry that holds together.

bakeries.name: Bryants Bakery Cafe
bakeries.hours: Weekdays from 6 am, Sun from 8 am
bakeries.why: Auburn St. Pies are hit and miss; the caramel slice is the standout.

bakeries.name: TBP Baking
bakeries.hours: Weekdays and Sat from 5 am, Sun from 9 am
bakeries.why: New on Auburn St with only a handful of reviews.

bakeries.name: Bryants Pies
bakeries.hours: Weekdays from 6 am, Sat 7 am, Sun 10 am
bakeries.why: Flaky pies and sausage rolls; reviews are uneven.

bakeries.name: Bakers Delight Lanyon
bakeries.hours: Daily 7 am to 7 pm
bakeries.why: In the car park, open early. Fresh rolls and cheese and bacon scrolls for the tank bag.

bakeries.name: Under (Mawson)
bakeries.hours: Wed to Sun 8 am to 2 pm
bakeries.why: Canberra’s cult pick. Cardamom buns and focaccia; queues and daily sell-outs.

bakeries.name: L’épi Artisan Bakery (Chisholm)
bakeries.hours: Daily 7 am to 2:30 pm
bakeries.why: Artisan bread, flaky pastries and well-reviewed pies, with Ona coffee.

bakeries.name: The Continental Cake Shop (Greenway)
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 8 am to 7 pm, weekends 9 am to 6 pm
bakeries.why: Celebration cakes and slices; strong on black forest and red velvet.

bakeries.name: Dobinsons (Greenway)
bakeries.hours: Daily from 7:30 am
bakeries.why: Reliable pies, sausage rolls and vanilla slice in the Southpoint centre.

bakeries.name: Tharwa General Store and Clarries cafe
bakeries.hours: Daily 9 am to 5:30 pm
bakeries.why: Built in 1922. Steak and pepper pies and lamingtons reviewers call the best they’ve had. Opens after we pass, so note it for another day.

bakeries.name: Clementine Bakery
bakeries.hours: Thu to Sun 8:30 am to 2 pm
bakeries.why: Five sourdoughs, croissants, sausage rolls and lamingtons, with seats under the old balcony on Comur St.

bakeries.name: Yass Country Kitchen
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri from 5 am, Sat from 8 am, closed Sun
bakeries.why: Locals call its chunky beef pies the best in town. Can be short-staffed around lunch.

bakeries.name: Yass Valley Bakery
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 9 am to 2 pm
bakeries.why: Three bakers on site, big gluten-free range. Reviews are mixed on price; the chunky beef pie gets the praise.

bakeries.name: The Yass Cafe
bakeries.hours: Daily 6:30 am to 3 pm
bakeries.why: Not a bakery, but the best-rated coffee on Comur St for those who just want a brew.

bakeries.name: The Bakery Boorowa
bakeries.hours: Daily from 6 am (Sat 7, Sun 8) to 4 pm
bakeries.why: Oversized country bakes, pepper pies and a huge eclair, with plenty of seating.

bakeries.name: Mick’s Local Bakery
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 7 am to 2 pm, Sat 7:30 am to 1 pm
bakeries.why: Bourbon and honey chicken and pepper pies, jalapeño sausage rolls, very friendly service.

bakeries.name: Royce’s Homestyle Cakes
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 6 am to 3 pm, Sat 7 am to 1 pm
bakeries.why: Proper baked custard tarts and fresh sandwiches. Cash only and inconsistent reviews.

bakeries.name: Hutchison’s Bakehouse
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri from 5 am (Mon 6) to 3 pm, Sat to 1 pm
bakeries.why: Big raspberry-and-cream lamingtons and good coffee. The cakes outshine the pies.

bakeries.name: Ironbark Espresso
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 5:30 am to 2 pm, weekends 7 am to noon
bakeries.why: Cafe, not a bakery, but its slices (try the sour cream apple) are worth a look.

bakeries.name: Millthorpe Providore
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 6 am to 3 pm, weekends 7 am to 3 pm
bakeries.why: 23 Victoria St. A 5/5 sausage roll, fruit loaf and Seven Miles coffee. Right by the motel.

bakeries.name: The Old Mill Cafe
bakeries.hours: Wed to Sun 7 am to 2 pm
bakeries.why: Cakes and a lemon meringue pie that sells out fast.

bakeries.name: Millthorpe Sweets and Treats
bakeries.hours: From 10 am, closed Tue
bakeries.why: Handmade chocolates and German biscuits for the panniers.

bakeries.name: Carah’s Cakes & Pies
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 6 am to 4:30 pm, Sat to 1:30 pm, closed Sun
bakeries.why: Brisket, jalapeño and cheese pies; steak, bacon and cheese gets raves. Busy at lunch.

bakeries.name: FoodWeDo
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 6 am to 1 pm, Sat 7 am to 2 pm, Sun 8 am to 1 pm
bakeries.why: Everything baked on site; a local’s tip for the best pie in town. Pastries sell out early.

bakeries.name: Bernard’s Bakery
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 7 am to 4 pm, weekends 7 am to 3 pm
bakeries.why: Pepper steak pie and possibly the best banh mi west of the mountains.

bakeries.name: Village Bakehouse
bakeries.hours: Daily from 6 am
bakeries.why: Big, with an upstairs and a drive-thru. Signature beef pie and danishes.

bakeries.name: Bathurst French Hot Bread
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 6 am to 6 pm, Sat to 4 pm, closed Sun
bakeries.why: Go for the pork roll, not the pies. Card surcharge.

bakeries.name: Golden Sunshine Bakery
bakeries.hours: Daily 6 am to 5 pm
bakeries.why: Lithgow Valley centre. Cream horns, lamingtons and famous fruit mince tarts.

bakeries.name: El Latte Lithgow
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 5 am to 4 pm, weekends 7 am to 3 pm
bakeries.why: Cafe on Main St with homemade apple crumble and brownies.

bakeries.name: The Lithgow Tin Shed
bakeries.hours: Most days from 6:30 or 8 am to 3 pm
bakeries.why: Cafe; slow-cooked beef pie with mash and peas, good almond croissant.

bakeries.name: Chi Cong Hot Bread
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 6 am to 3:30 pm
bakeries.why: Pizza breads and sausage rolls; skip the pies. No coffee.

bakeries.name: Poles Patisserie
bakeries.hours: Daily 7:30 am to 5 pm (Sun 8 to 4)
bakeries.why: Westfield. Steak and kidney pie worth driving an hour for, plus scallop pies.

bakeries.name: La Bakehouse Cafe
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 6:30 am to 3 pm, weekends 7 am to 2:30 pm
bakeries.why: High St. Loaded steak, bacon and cheese pies at old-school prices.

bakeries.name: Profiterole Patisserie
bakeries.hours: Daily 6 am to 10 pm
bakeries.why: Opposite the station. Cakes, crepes and pastries; all halal.

bakeries.name: Penrith Pies and Pastries
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 7:30 am to 5 pm, Sat 8 am to 3 pm
bakeries.why: Jamisontown. The gluten-free option, including gluten-free banh mi.

bakeries.name: Taddy’s Cakes and Pies
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 6 am to 3 pm, Sat 7 am to 2 pm
bakeries.why: New and small. Beef and jalapeño pie and a great latte.

bakeries.name: Glen’s Bakery Cafe
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 5:30 am to 6 pm, weekends 6 am to 1 pm
bakeries.why: Timber shed cafe. Lamingtons with real cream, apple turnovers and gourmet pies.

bakeries.name: B85 Artisan Bakery
bakeries.hours: Thu to Sun 6:30 am to 2 pm
bakeries.why: Sourdough that beats Sonoma, according to locals. Crème brûlée tart and almond croissant.

bakeries.name: Lahaina Banh Mi & Pie
bakeries.hours: Daily 6 am to 4:30 pm
bakeries.why: Run by the original Le Bakery owner. Crispy pork rolls plus pies.

bakeries.name: Arta Atelier
bakeries.hours: Wed to Sun 8 am to 3 pm
bakeries.why: Fine patisserie tarts and choux. Listed in the Good Food Guide.

bakeries.name: Cafe Creme Della Creme
bakeries.hours: Mon to Fri 6:30 am to 4 pm, weekends shorter
bakeries.why: Gourmet buttery pies with huge beef chunks. Recent reviews mixed.

bakeries.name: Saint Nicks Patisserie
bakeries.hours: Mon to Sat 7:30 am to 4 pm
